To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CQ yields a high degree of internal variation, that risk preferences are positively related to the size of the risky shift, and that the seriousness of the consequences of failure are negatively related to the size and to the riskiness of the recommendations.

the risk preference measure (the Choice-dilemmas Questionaire) is a valid and reliable measure of risk proness, that risk proneness varies from individual to individual, and that risk preference and risk-taking are related.

the CQ items are not all equally related to risk preference and to the degree of shift toward risky recommendations; the degree of shift and risk preference are both related to seriousness of consequences; and the degree of shift is inversely related to seriousness of consequence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between risk preference, consequences of failure and the magnitude of risky shift.
the question of whether there is any relationship between the degree of risk proneness and the degree of shift toward risky choices.
the development of a measure of risk preferences that is more sensitive to individual differences than the Choice-Dilemmas Questionnaire.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Choice-dilemmas Questionnaires, and other risk measures, do not measure risk preference.

the Choice-Dilemmas Questionnaire is an excellent measure of the risk preferences that people have in situations where they are not required to act, but that these risk preferences have little to do with the degree of shift that occurs when they are required to act.
the CQ is a valid and reliable measure of risk preference, and that the risk preference measure is a valid and useful measure for research in the area of risky shift.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
risk proneness is a function of the seriousness of the consequences of failure.
the usual measure of risk preference is not a unitary construct and that the degree to which a person is risk prone is related to the consequences of failure in a situation.
risk preference is related to both risk taking and to seriousness of consequences of risk, but not to degree of shift toward or against risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
risk preferences can be understood in terms of a trade-off between the potential gains from risk taking and the potential losses from failure.
the C-DQ may not be measuring the same thing across different contexts.
the C-DQ is not a unitary measure of risk proness, and that its use as such is unwarranted.
